::: {#def-adjacency-matrix}
#### Adjacency matrix

Let $G$ be a graph (@def-graph-vertices-edges) or a directed graph (@def-directed-graph),
and list its vertices in a chosen order as $v_1, \ldots, v_n$.
The **adjacency matrix** of $G$ [@wikipedia_adjacency_matrix] is the $n \times n$ matrix (@def-matrix) $A_G$
whose entry $a_{ij}$ in row $i$ and column $j$ is

- if $G$ is a graph, the number of edges with endpoints $v_i$ and $v_j$;
- if $G$ is a directed graph, the number of edges from $v_i$ to $v_j$.

So a loop at $v_i$ adds 1 to the diagonal entry $a_{ii}$.

:::
